How words guide and reassure. The skill's voice work lives in [[copy-voice]].

- **Microcopy** — the small text (labels, errors, placeholders) that outsizes its length in how trustworthy a product feels. → [[copy-voice]]
- **CTA** — the primary action label; "Save changes" outperforms "Submit." Own the action, don't apologise for it. → [[copy-voice]]
- **Error message** — name what went wrong and how to fix it; "Invalid input" names nothing. → [[forms-validation]]
- **Placeholder** — hint text that vanishes on typing; it cannot replace a label — the reminder is gone when needed.
- **Sentence case** — cap only the first word and proper nouns — the UI default; capitalising Every Word gives microcopy a stiff, contractual tone.

- **10–16 s per loop, 3–5 beats** building to a payoff; one gesture and a response can be enough. A second scene earns its length only with a new outcome or surface, never the same beat twice.
- **Open on a finished screen that works as a still**; the first real content is there before the first beat.
- **The payoff is visible at shown size** (a panel, a window coming forward, a clear state change) and **arrives full** — never a blank surface for a quarter second.
- **A satellite arrives at the beat it pays off**, carrying its payload, or is present from frame one in a reserved column.
- **The poster is the frame most people see** (a thumbnail, reduced motion, a screenshot). Set it to the beat that tells the story on its own, with the result left on screen. Never a frame caught mid-change: a digit mid-roll held still reads as a glitch.
- **Motion without hierarchy is cut.** Cover each moving element in turn; if the story is clearer without it, it goes.

- Good: `{ "id": "s2-chip", "kind": "click", "t": 2.34, "x": 1500, "y": 300, "w": 120, "h": 120 }`. The contact frame is 2.00 + 0.85 x 0.4 s; `--report` should then read the onset at 2.350 s (the default 10 ms lag), ~4.4 kHz (the click band, 2600 + 2600 x 0.5^0.5, inside 2.8 to 5.2 kHz) and pan +0.39 ((1500 / 1920 - 0.5) x 1.4). As a dry-register `land`, the same box would voice ~3.1 kHz (5200 x 0.5^0.75) with t60 ~230 ms.

Gold example: `docs/demo/hyperframes/assets/sfx/cues.json`, 138 cues in register B (83 clicks, 14 thuds, a bed in F with dropouts before the name), rendered by `skills/design-engineering/scripts/sound-sheet.mjs`.
Check: one cause per onset. Every line of `--report` names a cue id you can point at in the film as a move the eye tracks, on its frame or up to two after; an onset you cannot point at is cut. This carries into sound Benji Taylor's Stageshow rule that every motion has a cause.

[DiceBear](https://www.dicebear.com/) is an open-source library that generates SVG avatars from a string seed (usually the user's id, email, or name). Same seed always produces the same avatar — so users see the same generated face every visit.

- 30+ style packs (`adventurer`, `bottts`, `lorelei`, `pixel-art`, etc.).
- HTTP API: `https://api.dicebear.com/9.x/<style>/svg?seed=<seed>`.
- NPM packages: `@dicebear/core` + `@dicebear/<style>` for self-hosting.
- Open source: [github.com/dicebear/dicebear](https://github.com/dicebear/dicebear) and [github.com/dicebear/styles](https://github.com/dicebear/styles).
- License: most styles are CC0 / free; a few designer-contributed styles have specific terms — check per style.

nse.
- **Focus under sticky chrome** — `scroll-padding-block-start` on the scroller equal to the header's height; `-block-end` for a sticky footer or cookie bar ([[growth-and-overflow]]).
- **Zoom** — never `maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no`; the iOS input-zoom fix is a 16px input, not a locked viewport ([[forms-behavior]]). Text boxes take `min-height`, never `height`. Write media queries in `rem` so a larger browser font size reaches the narrow layout.
- **Forced colours** — Windows High Contrast drops every `box-shadow`. A shadow ring keeps `border: 1px solid transparent` under it so an edge still draws; never `forced-color-adjust: none` without checking the control stays visible.
- **Timed UI** — auto-dismiss only low-stakes confirmations. A toast carrying an action, an error or something the user may need stays until dismissed; one that must time out gets ≥ 5 s and pauses while hovered or focused. An undo link that vanishes on a timer is data loss on a schedule.
